questions.stem: The law of conservation of energy states that energy:

options.text: Cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred between stores
Is always lost as heat during any process
Can be destroyed but not created
Can be created but not destroyed

questions.explanation: The law of conservation of energy states that energy cannot be created or destroyed. It can only be transferred from one store to another or transformed from one type to another.

questions.stem: A ball is dropped from a height with no air resistance. At the halfway point:

options.text: All its energy is gravitational potential
It has equal amounts of GPE and KE

questions.explanation: Without air resistance, GPE lost equals KE gained. At the halfway point, half the GPE has been converted to KE, so they are equal.

options.text: A system with no moving parts
A system where no energy enters or leaves
A system that only uses renewable energy
A system where all energy is kinetic

questions.explanation: A closed system is one where no energy enters or leaves. In a closed system, the total energy remains constant.

questions.stem: A 2 kg ball falls from 5 m (g = 10 N/kg). What is its speed just before hitting the ground (no air resistance)?
questions.explanation: Using conservation of energy: mgh = 1/2 mv^2, so v = sqrt(2gh) = sqrt(2 x 10 x 5) = sqrt(100) = 10 m/s.

questions.stem: When a ball slides down a rough slope, the total energy at the bottom is:

options.text: The same as at the top
Less than at the top because energy has been destroyed

questions.explanation: The total energy is always conserved. On a rough slope, some GPE is converted to thermal energy instead of KE, but the total energy remains the same.

questions.stem: Which equation represents energy conservation for a falling object with no air resistance?
questions.explanation: For a falling object with no air resistance, GPE lost = KE gained, giving mgh = 1/2 mv^2.

questions.stem: Energy that is 'wasted' during a process has been:

options.text: Dissipated to the surroundings and is no longer useful

questions.explanation: Wasted energy is not destroyed. It is dissipated (spread out) to the surroundings, usually as thermal energy, and becomes too spread out to be useful.
